ai_assessment.method: Full direct English-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 1518 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported nine major and one hundred and seven minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.69; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: ‘Far the best ending’ (by far the best) was inverted into ‘far from the best’; corrected.
James’s line to Sibyl was addressed to the wrong person (‘Con nghĩ Sibyl…’); now ‘Anh nghĩ em…’.
The clause ‘she had marred him for a moment, if he had wounded her for an age’ was left dangling by a bare ‘nếu’; corrected.
The long dawn sentence of chapter XI was calqued into near-unreadable Vietnamese; rewritten.
Frankincense and aloes were both ‘trầm hương’; now ‘nhũ hương’ and ‘trầm hương’.
Three relative clauses in the Renaissance catalogue were syntactically broken; rewritten.
Gautier’s French verse was flat prose; now twelve lines of Vietnamese verse with a regular rhythm and rhymes.
Lady Narborough’s jokes were carried over literally with a gloss; now Vietnamese idioms and a pun that keep the joke.
Every em dash of the English in the last four chapters was dropped; all were restored.
The women who braved censure for Dorian’s sake were turned into Dorian defying censure; corrected after the last blind review, by hand.
Two lines of the Gautier verse have seven syllables where the French has eight, and a few rhyme words are fillers.
The bonnet in Lady Narborough’s first clause no longer has a referent after the idiom swap.
Narration calls Alan Campbell ‘ông’ in a few units where ‘anh ta’ is the rule.

summary: Full assessment of all 1,518 English/Vietnamese passages: the Preface, twenty chapter headings and every paragraph (about 79,000 words of English). The first reviews of seven ranges scored 8.53, 8.85, 8.48, 8.28, 8.45, 8.75 and 8.47 and found nine majors (an epigram inverted, a wrong addressee, a dangling clause, a calqued dawn sentence, frankincense and aloes confused, a broken catalogue, Gautier’s verse in flat prose, Lady Narborough’s jokes lost, and every em dash dropped in the last chapters); one round of fixes with book-wide rules and fresh separate-context blind reviews of the five ranges with majors then scored 8.80, 8.73, 8.80, 8.63 and 8.85, with the two ranges that had passed (8.85 and 8.75) given a minors-only polish; range 5 needed a second fix and a third review (8.63), whose one remaining major (an inverted subject in unit 881) was fixed by hand without a further blind review. The final score is taken from the weakest range, 8.63 on the half-point scale, above the unchanged 8.6 threshold. Open minors include two verse lines one syllable short, a bonnet without a referent in unit 1080 and a few ‘ông’ for Alan Campbell.

title_review.target_title: Bức chân dung của Dorian Gray
title_review.rationale: The title is rendered as ‘Bức chân dung của Dorian Gray’ (the portrait of Dorian Gray); no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.
